youtube.title: Taiwan: The 130 km Strait the World Fears a War Over
youtube.description:
An island smaller than Switzerland held 92% of the world's most advanced chipmaking capacity in 2019. It sits 130 km off China and is ringed by military drills. Why has Taiwan become the place major powers plan around, and who has the stronger case?

On the map: the strait, the first island chain and the ports, the lines drawn in 1895, 1945, 1955 and 1979, Beijing's case and Taipei's case in their own words, and three ways the map could change: a quarantine, an invasion, or a line that holds while the chips move abroad.

{CHAPTERS}

youtube.comment: Should the world's most advanced chips be made in one place, or spread out even if it costs more? 👇

sources.claim: In 2019 Taiwan held 92% of the world's chipmaking capacity below 10 nm, South Korea 8%
sources.source: Boston Consulting Group & Semiconductor Industry Association, 'Strengthening the Global Semiconductor Supply Chain in an Uncertain Era', April 2021

sources.claim: In August 2022, Chinese missiles landed in the waters around Taiwan; six exercise zones after Nancy Pelosi's visit
sources.source: Xinhua announcement of exercise zones, 2 Aug 2022; Taiwan Ministry of National Defense and Japan Ministry of Defense statements, 4 Aug 2022

sources.claim: The strait is about 130 km wide at its narrowest, Pingtan to the coast near Hsinchu
sources.source: Great-circle measurement for this episode, 25.45N 119.85E to 24.85N 120.90E (~126-136 km); commonly given as about 130 km (Reuters, 2022-2024 reporting)

sources.claim: Bloomberg Economics: a war over Taiwan would cost about $10 trillion, roughly a tenth of world output; a blockade about 5% of world output
sources.source: Bloomberg Economics, 'War over Taiwan would cost world economy $10 trillion', 9 Jan 2024

sources.claim: Taiwan is smaller than Switzerland
sources.source: Taiwan Ministry of the Interior (about 36,197 km²); Swiss Federal Statistical Office (41,285 km²)

sources.claim: Taiwan covers about 36,000 km² and has 23.4 million people
sources.source: Taiwan Ministry of the Interior, population statistics, end-2024

sources.claim: Yushan rises to 3,952 metres
sources.source: Taiwan Yushan National Park Headquarters

sources.claim: Yonaguni is about 110 km from Taiwan's east coast
sources.source: Yonaguni Town Office / Japan Ministry of Defense (111 km)

sources.claim: Y'Ami, the Philippines' northernmost island, lies about 140 km south of Taiwan's southern tip
sources.source: Great-circle measurement for this episode, Eluanbi 21.90N 120.85E to Y'Ami 21.12N 121.95E

sources.claim: US strategists have spoken of a first island chain since the 1950s
sources.source: Andrew Erickson & Joel Wuthnow, 'Barriers, Springboards and Benchmarks', The China Quarterly, 2016 (traces the term to John Foster Dulles, 1951)

sources.claim: The strait is one of the busiest container lanes: nearly half the global container fleet passed through it in 2022
sources.source: Bloomberg analysis of ship-tracking data, August 2022

sources.claim: $2.45 trillion of goods passed through the Taiwan Strait in 2022, over a fifth of global maritime trade
sources.source: CSIS ChinaPower, 'Crossroads of Commerce: How the Taiwan Strait Propels the Global Economy', 2024

sources.claim: TSMC was founded in Hsinchu in 1987; its leading plants are in Hsinchu, Taichung and Tainan
sources.source: TSMC Annual Report 2024

sources.claim: Taiwan imports about 97% of its energy
sources.source: Taiwan Energy Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Energy Statistics Handbook 2023

sources.claim: Most LNG arrives at terminals in Taichung and Kaohsiung (Yong'an)
sources.source: CPC Corporation Taiwan, LNG terminal information, 2024

sources.claim: Kinmen lies about 10 km from Xiamen; Matsu lies off Fuzhou; both governed by Taipei
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Kinmen Island' and 'Matsu Islands'

sources.claim: Dutch traders built a fort near today's Tainan in 1624
sources.source: Tonio Andrade, 'How Taiwan Became Chinese', Columbia University Press, 2008

sources.claim: The Qing took Taiwan in 1683 and named it a province in 1885
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Taiwan: History'

sources.claim: Treaty of Shimonoseki, 17 April 1895, ceded 'the island of Formosa' to Japan; Japanese rule for 50 years
sources.source: Treaty of Shimonoseki, Article 2, 17 April 1895

sources.claim: Cairo, 1943: Formosa to be 'restored to the Republic of China'
sources.source: Cairo Declaration, 1 Dec 1943 (US Department of State, Foreign Relations of the United States)

sources.claim: The Republic of China took over Taiwan's administration on 25 October 1945
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Taiwan: History'; Taiwan Executive Yuan

sources.claim: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic on 1 October 1949; the ROC government moved to Taipei in December 1949
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Chinese Civil War'; ROC Executive Yuan decision, 7 Dec 1949

sources.claim: ROC troops stopped a landing at Guningtou on Kinmen in October 1949
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Kinmen Island'; ROC Ministry of National Defense history

sources.claim: Truman ordered the Seventh Fleet into the strait in June 1950, to prevent any attack on Formosa, and called on the government on Formosa to cease air and sea operations against the mainland
sources.source: Statement by President Truman on the situation in Korea, 27 June 1950 (Truman Library)

sources.claim: In the 1951 peace treaty Japan renounced 'all right, title and claim to Formosa', without naming a recipient
sources.source: Treaty of Peace with Japan (San Francisco), Article 2(b), 8 Sept 1951

sources.claim: By most accounts US Air Force general Benjamin Davis Jr. drew the median line in 1955
sources.source: Taipei Times, 'Median line explained', 2020; Defense News reporting, 2020

sources.claim: The PLA shelled Kinmen for weeks from 23 August 1958; Kinmen stayed under Taipei's control
sources.source: US Department of State, Office of the Historian, 'The Taiwan Strait Crises: 1954-55 and 1958'; Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Kinmen Island'

sources.claim: UN Resolution 2758, 25 Oct 1971, gave China's seat to the People's Republic and expelled 'the representatives of Chiang Kai-shek'
sources.source: UN General Assembly Resolution 2758 (XXVI), 25 Oct 1971

sources.claim: 1972: the US acknowledged that Chinese on either side 'maintain there is but one China and that Taiwan is a part of China' and 'does not challenge that position'
sources.source: Joint Communiqué (Shanghai Communiqué), 28 Feb 1972

sources.claim: On 1 January 1979 the US recognised Beijing and ended formal ties with Taipei
sources.source: Joint Communiqué on the Establishment of Diplomatic Relations, effective 1 Jan 1979

sources.claim: The Taiwan Relations Act calls non-peaceful means, 'including by boycotts or embargoes', of 'grave concern' and provides 'arms of a defensive character'
sources.source: Taiwan Relations Act, Public Law 96-8, Section 2(b), 10 April 1979

sources.claim: By 2024, 12 governments, counting the Holy See, recognised Taipei
sources.source: Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, list of diplomatic allies, after Nauru's switch on 15 Jan 2024

sources.claim: Martial law ended in 1987; first direct presidential election in 1996
sources.source: Taiwan Presidential Office; Central Election Commission, 23 March 1996

sources.claim: In March 1996 China fired missiles into zones off Keelung and Kaohsiung; the US sent two carrier groups
sources.source: US Department of State, Office of the Historian; Congressional Research Service report RL30341

sources.claim: Beijing says Taiwan has belonged to China 'since ancient times'
sources.source: PRC Taiwan Affairs Office & State Council Information Office, white paper 'The Taiwan Question and China's Reunification in the New Era', 10 Aug 2022

sources.claim: Most of the world's governments recognise the People's Republic as China's sole government
sources.source: PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of diplomatic relations (over 180 states), 2024

sources.claim: Anti-Secession Law, 14 March 2005, Article 8: 'non-peaceful means' if peaceful reunification is 'completely exhausted'
sources.source: Anti-Secession Law of the PRC, Article 8, 14 March 2005

sources.claim: Xi Jinping, 2022: 'we will never promise to renounce the use of force'
sources.source: Report to the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, 16 Oct 2022

sources.claim: The People's Republic has never governed Taiwan; the island has its own government, army and currency since 1949
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Taiwan'; Congressional Research Service, 'Taiwan: Political and Security Issues', 2024

sources.claim: Lai Ching-te: the two are 'not subordinate to each other'
sources.source: Inaugural address of President Lai Ching-te, 20 May 2024
Election Study Center, National Chengchi University, Taiwanese/Chinese identity trend, 1992-2024

sources.claim: The Kuomintang favours more talks with Beijing; the DPP stresses Taiwan's separate rule
sources.source: Party platforms of the KMT and DPP; Congressional Research Service, 2024

sources.claim: CIA director William Burns: Xi instructed the PLA to be 'ready by 2027 to conduct an invasion', not a decision
sources.source: William Burns, remarks at Georgetown University, 2 Feb 2023

sources.claim: In November 2025 Japan's prime minister told parliament a Taiwan emergency could be a 'survival-threatening situation'; Beijing protested
sources.source: Sanae Takaichi, House of Representatives Budget Committee, 7 Nov 2025; PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs statements, Nov 2025

sources.claim: China's foreign ministry has said there is no 'median line'
sources.source: PRC Foreign Ministry spokesperson Wang Wenbin, press conference, 21 Sept 2020

sources.claim: Joint Sword-2024A drills followed Lai's inauguration in May 2024
sources.source: PLA Eastern Theater Command announcement, 23 May 2024

sources.claim: Record 153 Chinese military aircraft around Taiwan in one day, October 2024
sources.source: Taiwan Ministry of National Defense, statement, 15 Oct 2024

sources.claim: Strait Thunder-2025A practised blockading key ports and energy routes
sources.source: PLA Eastern Theater Command announcement, 2 April 2025

sources.claim: China's official 2025 defence budget about $249 billion (1.78 trillion yuan); Taiwan planned about $20 billion (NT$647 billion)
sources.source: PRC Ministry of Finance budget report, 5 March 2025; Taiwan Executive Yuan 2025 budget proposal, Aug 2024

sources.claim: SIPRI and the US Defense Department estimate China spends more than its official figure; SIPRI: $314 billion in 2024
sources.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database fact sheet, April 2025; US DoD, 'Military and Security Developments Involving the PRC', Dec 2024

sources.claim: Both Beijing and Taipei say they seek peace
sources.source: Xi Jinping, Report to the 20th Party Congress, 16 Oct 2022 ('peaceful reunification'); Lai Ching-te, inaugural address, 20 May 2024 ('war has no winners')

sources.claim: A quarantine by China's coast guard is one studied scenario
sources.source: CSIS, 'How China Could Quarantine Taiwan', 5 June 2024

sources.claim: Taiwan's LNG stocks reported at about 11 days of use
sources.source: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs figures reported by Reuters, 2024

sources.claim: Ian Easton counted 14 beaches suitable for a large landing; weather windows in April and October
sources.source: Ian Easton, 'The Chinese Invasion Threat', Project 2049 Institute, 2017

sources.claim: CSIS ran the invasion 24 times; in most runs it failed, at high cost to all sides
sources.source: CSIS, 'The First Battle of the Next War: Wargaming a Chinese Invasion of Taiwan', 9 Jan 2023

sources.claim: TSMC opened a plant in Kumamoto in February 2024 and began volume production in Arizona in late 2024
sources.source: JASM opening ceremony, 24 Feb 2024; TSMC Q4 2024 earnings call, 16 Jan 2025

sources.claim: Some argue spreading chip production lowers the world's exposure to one place
sources.source: US CHIPS and Science Act, 9 Aug 2022, and US Commerce Department statements on supply-chain resilience, 2022-2024

sources.claim: Others argue Taiwan's chip industry is its best protection (the 'silicon shield')
sources.source: Craig Addison, 'Silicon Shield: Taiwan's Protection Against Chinese Attack', Fultus, 2001

sources.claim: Much of China's imported oil passes the Strait of Malacca
sources.source: US Energy Information Administration, 'World Oil Transit Chokepoints', 2024
